summary: Affinity mismatch and unexpected fallback after proactive dedicated capacity rebalance
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that after a proactive capacity rebalance on Dedicated pool 'dp-usw-2' their sessions lost model-version affinity and were routed to the fallback variant mid-request. This caused two user-facing failures: an aborted streaming response and a degraded generation quality for multi-turn chat flows.

Impact:
- BrightPath Health observed ~0.6% of requests (sampled from their edge logs) diverted to fallback variants over a 12-minute window.
- Several long-running streamed calls were terminated with a 502 when KV cache mismatches were detected.
- Customer production workload (SLA tier: Dedicated, critical) experienced increased latency and a handful of user-visible regressions.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-usw-2 (proactive rebalance at 2026-03-10T21:14:05Z)
- Edge region: us-west (primary), failover to us-east observed
- Models: redwood/rw-instruct-13b-quant-v2 pinned on tenant route; fallback: redwood/rw-chat-7b

Steps to reproduce (observed in customer traffic):
1) Customer pinned route to rw-instruct-13b-quant-v2 and validated affinity for 48 hours.
2) Autoscaler triggered proactive rebalance to migrate GPUs in dp-usw-2 for maintenance.
3) Edge control-plane initiated graceful drain on 4 nodes; routing tokens were reissued.
4) A subset of long-lived sessions (session_cookie present) resumed across the new node and received a routing decision referencing the fallback model variant.

Expected behavior:
- Pinned sessions maintain version affinity across proactive capacity changes, or are gracefully failed with a clear error to the application.

Actual behavior:
- A subset of pinned sessions lost affinity and were silently routed to fallback variants midstream. Streaming connections returned 502/5xx for some connections where KV cache state mismatch was detected.

Immediate customer-visible workaround applied:
- Support temporarily set an edge-route-level policy to 'force-pin: true' for BrightPath to prevent rebind during subsequent rebalances.

Notes:
- This reproduces only for long-lived sessions that cross a node migration boundary while the edge-router is applying routing token rotations.
- We observed header mutation in the sidecar for some requests that correlates with affinity loss.
steps_to_reproduce: Pin route to target model and run multi-turn streaming sessions for >300s
Trigger proactive rebalance / simulate node drain on dedicated pool
Observe whether resumed sessions receive original pin or fallback decision
Check edge-router logs for token rotation and header mutations
logs: 2026-03-10T21:15:07Z sidecar[svc]: header-mutation: removed x-rw-affinity-token for request id=req-9f8a
2026-03-10T21:15:09Z serving-runtime: fallback-route-elected tenant=brightpath route=/v1/chat model=rw-chat-7b status=200
Log snippets and full traces uploaded to S3: s3://rwi-support/traces/SUP-450321/
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: token rotation race where edge-router issues new routing token before scheduler completes node handoff, causing sidecars to read inconsistent mapping.
Hypothesis 2: sidecar header sanitizer inadvertently strips affinity header during in-flight migration when certain header TTLs expire.
KV cache mismatch errors in serving-runtime align with rebind window timestamps.
No evidence of model-serving binary regression in rw-instruct-13b-quant-v2; quant kernels load and init completed successfully on new node.
Reproducer run in staging with traffic replay shows ~0.3% session-affinity loss on drains when edge-router rotation delay set to 50-150ms.
resolution: Workaround: Applied 'force-pin: true' on the tenant's route to prevent automatic rebind during planned rebalances and scheduled a short maintenance window. Engineering mitigation: edge-router patch to serialize token-rotate with node-handback confirmed as PR #2123. Next steps: merge PR, deploy canary to staging, then promote to prod with a focused observability check for affinity headers. Postmortem to recommend a coordinated token rotation protocol for proactive rebalances.
